title: Mirabel and the Confession
premise: Zephyrine Oyelaran, a night dispatcher who has spent fifteen years cataloguing the town of Marrow Creek's secrets, receives an anonymous prepayment from a client asking her to prove that a murder has not yet happened — the murder of councilman Elias Vann, scheduled by rumor for the anniversary of a drowning everyone believes was an accident. Following dispatch logs she alone kept, Zeph discovers the 'closed' case of drowned teenager Corinne Ashe was a cover-up involving the police chief and the taxi company's founder, and that someone is now killing everyone who touched those files. To stop the final murder — her own name is next on the list — Zeph must abandon her invisibility, expose the confession hidden in fifteen years of call records, and choose between justice through exposure or survival through silence. In the end she broadcasts the confession over the taxi radio band on the night of the anniversary, letting the whole town hear what it paid to forget.
about_author: Wendell Delacroix is the pen name of a former small-town records clerk who spent a decade reading other people's paperwork before writing about the people behind it. Delacroix lives off-grid in the northern hills and answers mail only by postcard.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Third-person limited from Zephyrine Oyelaran. On a slow night shift, Zeph introduces her meticulous system of logging every fare, caller, and secret that passes through Marrow Creek Taxi. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness — order as armor. A strange prepaid booking arrives: a client wants proof that a murder will not happen, dated three weeks out.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Zeph's POV. She traces the payment to a shell account and finds only one instruction: confirm that Elias Vann dies of natural causes on October 9th, or refund nothing. The beat is unease sharpening into obsession; Zeph realizes the request implies a murder already planned — or already committed once before.

chapters.title: Corinne Ashe, 2009
chapters.summary: Alternating between Zeph's present and fragments of old dispatch tapes. Zeph pulls the file on the night Corinne Ashe drowned, officially ruled accidental, and notices her own handwriting in the margin of a log she doesn't remember making. Beat: vertigo — the past has been edited, and possibly by her.

chapters.title: The Chief's Standing Fare
chapters.summary: Zeph's POV. Police Chief Dornan has taken the same taxi route every Friday for years — always to the reservoir. She tails the pattern and finds him meeting Vann, exchanging an envelope. Beat: dread mixed with the thrill of finally seeing the town's machinery instead of just recording it.

chapters.title: A Passenger Named Nobody
chapters.summary: A young drifter, Teo, becomes a recurring late-night passenger and begins asking questions about the reservoir road. Zeph's POV. His curiosity mirrors hers but lacks caution, and she warns him off too harshly. Beat: reluctant tenderness — the first crack in her isolation.

chapters.title: What the Founder Kept
chapters.summary: Zeph breaks into the archive of Aldous Merrick, the taxi company's dead founder, and finds a second ledger — parallel to hers — recording fares never dispatched: witnesses moved, bodies driven, payments logged. Beat: cold horror as she understands the company was the town's getaway service.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter in Zeph's POV reconstructing how she came to Marrow Creek fleeing her own erased identity, and why Merrick hired a woman who wanted to be unfindable. Beat: grief and complicity — she was hired precisely because she understood hiding.

chapters.title: The First Refund
chapters.summary: Merrick's former accountant is found dead in his car at the depot, staged as carbon monoxide poisoning. Zeph's POV realizes every person named in the second ledger is being crossed off. Beat: terror converting mystery into countdown.

chapters.title: Teo Knows Too Much
chapters.summary: Teo reveals he is Corinne Ashe's younger brother, grown and returned under another name, and that he sent the prepaid request to force the truth open. Zeph's POV. Beat: betrayal braided with recognition — they are both orphans of the same lie.

chapters.title: Dornan Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Chief Dornan visits the depot, friendly and lethal, letting Zeph know her logs have been read. He offers her a promotion and a warning in the same breath. Beat: suffocating menace; invisibility offered back to her like a bribe.

chapters.title: The Reservoir at Low Water
chapters.summary: Zeph and Teo dive the drought-shallowed reservoir and find Corinne's bicycle, zip-tied, weighted — evidence of murder, not accident. Beat: grim vindication curdling into fear, because retrieving it means someone can prove they were there.

chapters.title: Someone Is Editing Me
chapters.summary: Zeph discovers entries missing from her own ledgers — pages cut cleanly, matching her memory gaps. Her POV fractures between certainty and self-doubt. Beat: psychological unraveling; the question shifts from whodunit to who made me forget.

chapters.title: Vann's Confession Tape
chapters.summary: Teo produces a cassette Vann recorded years ago as insurance against Dornan and Merrick: a partial confession naming the driver who took Corinne to the water. Zeph's POV. Beat: electric hope — until they realize the tape names a driver still alive, still driving.

chapters.title: Route 9, Every Night
chapters.summary: The named driver is Ruthie Calloway, the depot's beloved day dispatcher, who has been quietly paying hush money for fifteen years. Zeph confronts her. Beat: tragic humanity — Ruthie claims she was told Corinne was already dying when she drove her.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Booking
chapters.summary: With four days left, the anonymous account books a final ride: pickup at the depot, destination the reservoir, passenger unnamed. Zeph's POV decodes the route and realizes the intended victim is herself. Beat: icy clarity — the prepayment was always her obituary.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Ghosts
chapters.summary: Zeph spends a sleepless day cross-referencing both ledgers and reconstructs the full chain: Merrick ordered it, Dornan covered it, Ruthie drove, and Vann — then a junior clerk — filed the false report that made him mayor-track. Beat: terrible completeness; the whole town fits inside one filing cabinet.

chapters.title: Ruthie Runs
chapters.summary: Panicked by the investigation, Ruthie flees with the original ledger pages and is run off Route 9 by an unmarked car. Zeph reaches the wreck first and takes the pages; Ruthie survives long enough to whisper that Dornan wasn't in the car that night — someone else was. Beat: sacrifice and a new question.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Band
chapters.summary: Zeph realizes the anonymous payer's voiceprint matches recordings of Aldous Merrick — whose death was also falsified. He is alive, orchestrating the cleanup of his own crime from abroad. Beat: scale-shift; the case was never local, and neither is the danger.

chapters.title: October 8th
chapters.summary: Teo is taken by Dornan's men as bait to force Zeph to surrender the ledger and tape. Her POV. Beat: fury overriding fear — the invisible woman chooses to become unmistakably visible, walking into the station house with everything she has.

chapters.title: The Depot Standoff
chapters.summary: Climax. Zeph trades the 'confession' for Teo while secretly patching the tape and both ledgers into the taxi company's radio transmitter. As Dornan realizes the trap, Merrick's man arrives to erase them all; in the chaos, Dornan's own recorded words go out across every cab radio in Marrow Creek. Beat: cathartic detonation.

chapters.title: Everyone Was Listening
chapters.summary: The town wakes to its own confession playing from every dashboard. State investigators arrive; Dornan is arrested, Vann resigns and is indicted, and warrants go out for Merrick. Zeph's POV. Beat: raw, disorienting daylight — justice arriving not as triumph but as exposure.

chapters.title: Dispatch Closed
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Zeph testifies under her real name for the first time in fifteen years, then burns her private ledger of the town's secrets rather than archive them. She offers Teo a job answering phones — no logs kept. Final beat: identity chosen, not hidden; the switchboard goes quiet, and she lets it.
